title: How to Collect CDs
gist: A collector's guide that opens with data on the CD revival: Luminate says 2026 CD sales are up 16 percent, driven by K-pop collectible editions, with 16.3 million discs sold in H1 versus 900 million-plus at the turn of the millennium. The rest is practical advice on players, stores, storage and care.

insights.claim: Luminate's 2026 data shows overall CD sales up 16 percent year to date, driven by K-pop acts like BTS, Enhypen and ATEEZ whose collectible editions encourage fans to buy multiple copies.
insights.speaker: Orlando Mendiola
insights.so_what: Physical-format growth is a fandom-merch phenomenon, a monetisation lever for K-pop labels beyond streaming.
insights.locator: According to 2026 data from the entertainment industry

insights.claim: Excluding K-pop, disc sales would still have risen 6.7 percent, indicating a broader if smaller revival.
insights.speaker: Orlando Mendiola
insights.so_what: Underlying growth beyond K-pop suggests durable demand for physical formats among collectors.
insights.quote: if K-pop were taken out of the data, disc sales would’ve still increased 6.7 percent

insights.claim: The music industry sold 16.3 million discs in H1 2026, versus more than 900 million annually around the turn of the millennium, so the revival is from a very small base.
insights.speaker: Orlando Mendiola
insights.so_what: Physical revival is real but immaterial to total industry revenue compared to streaming.
insights.quote: The music industry sold 16.3 million discs in the first half of this year
insights.locator: Though the numbers show solid growth

insights.claim: CDs are increasingly bought as merch and collectibles that support the artist rather than as necessities to hear the songs, and only half of millennial and Gen Z CD collectors own a player.
insights.speaker: Orlando Mendiola
insights.so_what: Physical media value shifts from utility to fandom signalling, favouring artist-direct and limited-edition strategies.
insights.quote: CDs are looked at more as merch—collectibles that support the artist—than as necessities to hear the songs

insights.claim: The author attributes the CD surge to K-pop, backlash against streaming platforms' policies, and Gen Z drivers of hand-me-down cars without Bluetooth.
insights.speaker: Orlando Mendiola
insights.so_what: Streaming-policy backlash and ownership preference create a niche counter-trend to subscription models.
insights.locator: But now the CD is enjoying a surge

insights.claim: Vinyl first outsold CDs in 2022, and a deluxe CD of Madonna's Confessions II sold at $34 in July 2026, more than some vinyl pressings.
insights.speaker: Orlando Mendiola
insights.so_what: Deluxe CD pricing above vinyl shows pricing power on collectible physical editions.

insights.claim: Del Bravo Record Shop reports portable CD players flying off the shelves and a 12.6 percent rise in CD sales this year, and Hogwild Records reports book-style CD wallets sold out at its supplier.
insights.speaker: Jessica Campa, Del Bravo Record Shop
insights.so_what: Accessory and hardware shortages suggest supply chains are not scaled for the revival, a niche for hardware makers.
insights.quote: They’ve been flying off the shelves
insights.locator: Del Bravo Record Shop, one of the oldest

insights.claim: Independent record stores still carry CDs and add free posters, stickers and autographed copies at regular price during release week, an advantage over Amazon.
insights.speaker: Orlando Mendiola
insights.so_what: Indie retail differentiates through in-store extras, sustaining a channel against online giants.
insights.locator: The Record Store Is Still Your Friend

insights.claim: Discogs' free app with barcode scanning identifies exact pressings and current market value, and links to sellers, making it the collector's pricing tool.
insights.speaker: Orlando Mendiola
insights.so_what: Discogs sits as the price-discovery layer for physical-media collectibles.

insights.claim: Physical media is truly owned and on demand, whereas online streams may be temporary, which is the author's case for collecting.
insights.speaker: Orlando Mendiola
insights.so_what: Ownership-versus-access sentiment is a counter-narrative to streaming concentration risk.
insights.quote: while online streams may be temporary, the physical media we have will always be something we truly own
